source_fields.formulation: Find first-order stationarity of the true reduced objective $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}} f(x,y)$, where $f(x,y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, on unconstrained Euclidean spaces.

assumptions.description: Every component obeys the individual smoothness condition $\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(z^\prime)\|_2\le\beta\|z-z^\prime\|_2$ globally, with the same public beta.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

assumptions.description: Each component is continuously differentiable. Only the average dual function $f(x,\cdot)$ is required to be mu_y-strongly concave; individual components may be nonconcave in y. Thus the dual optimizer is unique and $\nabla\Phi(x)=\nabla_x f(x,y^\star(x))$.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

assumptions.description: The public initialization is $(0,0)$ with exact dual promise $y^\star(0)=0$ and primal gap $\Phi(0)-\inf\Phi\le\Delta$. The dimensions and n,beta,mu_y,Delta are public. Component gradients, query norms and dual optimizers away from the initial point need not be bounded.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

source_fields.operation: At an adaptively selected index i and arbitrary joint point, receive only the exact full joint gradient $\nabla f_i(x,y)$. The same index always identifies the same fixed component. One component call costs one unit and a full mean gradient costs n. There are no function values, Hessians, reduced gradients or free dual maximizers in this interface. The source lower bound is proved for the stronger packet $(f_i,\nabla f_i)$ and therefore applies to this gradient-only interface by discarding the extra value. The upper algorithms use only gradients.

operations.query_signature: The query domain and ordering stated in the oracle paragraphs.

source_fields.feasibility: Return any measurable primal point $\widehat x$, possibly unqueried and with unrestricted coordinate support. No dual point or certificate is required.

source_fields.base_expression: The error is $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|_2$. The expected-squared criterion and constant-probability criterion are separate views with separate resource semantics.

source_fields.budget: Count every selected component joint-gradient call, including initialization and repetition. In the expected-RMS view optimize worst-instance expected work with almost sure termination. In the probability view require a fixed cap on every path. Internal arithmetic and memory are free. The matched quantities take a worst case over finite dimensions.
